own_solution.law: Let A = sqrt(2) Vm/4 and d = 1.4 V. The instantaneous load voltage is max(A|sin(theta)| - d, 0). With alpha = asin(d/A), its average is (2/pi)[A cos(alpha) - d(pi/2 - alpha)]. At Vm = 230 V this gives 50.3759 V. Increasing Vm by 8, 14, and 21 V gives 52.1762, 53.5265, and 55.1019 V respectively.
assumptions: The stated sinusoidal supply, ideal transformer, constant diode drops, and absence of smoothing apply.
The resistive load has finite positive resistance.
The lamp supply is a separate circuit.
A supply increase made before measurement remains in effect during measurement.

notes: All certified numerical answers agree with integration over the conducting interval at the displayed precision. Load resistance enters the current relation and cancels when obtaining load voltage; all listed resistances are positive and admissible. The lamp circuit and completed earlier experiment have no dependency on the measured voltage under the stated ideal model.
